summary: No relevant testing skill found. Focused API + UI verification showed the core category visibility can be restored: after the admin UI rebalance, sync_running=false and all 22 categories returned at least 20 active listings. However the rebalance flow is not safely fixed/idempotent: an admin rerun with min_per_category=15 reclassified 673/950 listings and created 118 extra duplicates despite categories already having >=20, and the frontend min=20 click then created another 185 duplicates. This repeated duplicate growth is a remaining backend defect in the affected admin rebalance flow.

critical.issue: Rebalance is not idempotent. A moderate rerun with {min_per_category:15, clear_sync_flag:true} returned ok:true but reclassified 673 listings and duplicates_created=118 even though pre-check category filters already showed >=20 listings for every category. The subsequent frontend button run with min_per_category=20 created another 185 duplicate/top-up listings. Repeated admin use can inflate/duplicate the catalog.

minor.issue: Initial status contradicted the expected post-fix state: sync_running=true with message 'Running actor for 28 categories...' before manual rebalance. After rebalance it correctly returned sync_running=false.

integration_issues.issue: The UI button is visible and shows the emerald result card, but each tested click invoked a backend rebalance that created large numbers of additional duplicate/top-up listings rather than behaving idempotently.

action_items: Make POST /api/admin/listings/rebalance idempotent: repeated runs at the same/lower threshold should not keep reclassifying the same listings or creating new duplicate/top-up listings when category counts already satisfy the threshold.
Persist enough metadata on top-up duplicates (or use secondary_categories instead of cloning) so sparse categories do not lose their filled items on the next classifier pass.
Recheck Apify sync scheduler/state so preview does not show sync_running=true unexpectedly after the claimed stuck flag clear.
critical_code_review_comments: /app/backend/server.py:1553-1588 projects no existing secondary_categories and compares set(secondary_ids) to set([]), so any listing with computed secondary categories is counted/updated as reclassified on every run instead of comparing against current stored secondary_categories.

/app/backend/server.py:1617-1634 samples random donors for sparse categories and overwrites category_id; cloned/top-up listings can be reclassified away from the sparse category on the next rebalance, causing repeated duplicate creation. The variable orig_pri is assigned after category_id is overwritten and is not used to preserve the donor's original category.
seed_data_creation: No seed data was created. Testing invoked the real admin rebalance endpoint twice, which created 303 duplicate/top-up listings total (118 from API min_per_category=15, 185 from the frontend min_per_category=20 button). Current post-test state has sync_running=false and every category has >=20 visible active listings.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Current preview state after testing: /api/admin/sync/status sync_running=false; /api/listings?category_id=<id>&limit=96 returns >=20 for all 22 categories. Rebalance endpoint remains the concern: do not repeatedly click it unless testing idempotency, because it created many duplicates during this run.
rca_of_the_issue: Runtime evidence and code review indicate the rebalance pass is not comparing against existing secondary_categories and top-up clones are treated as normal listings by future classifier passes. When rebalanced again, many clones/listings move back to classifier-preferred categories, sparse categories fall below the requested threshold, and new duplicates are created to refill them. Reproduction: authenticate as admin, verify all categories have >=20, then POST /api/admin/listings/rebalance with a lower threshold such as 15; observe hundreds reclassified and duplicates_created >0.
